author: matiasfons
body:
## What

Adds an async `Authenticator` trait and `AuthPolicy::Custom(Arc<dyn Authenticator>)`
to `namidb-bolt`, so an embedder can verify HELLO/LOGON credentials against
an external source instead of the built-in `Open` / `Token` schemes.

`Session::authenticate` becomes async and, when `AuthPolicy::Custom` is set,
delegates to the authenticator with the full auth map (`scheme` / `principal`
/ `credentials`). `Open` and `Token` behaviour is unchanged, so `namidb-server`
is unaffected. A rejection still surfaces as
`Neo.ClientError.Security.Unauthorized`.

## Why

The NamiDB managed cloud terminates Bolt for many tenants and must
authenticate each connection against the control plane (API key → principal)
rather than a single static token. The `Backend` trait never sees the HELLO/
LOGON credentials, so auth has to be pluggable at the `Session` layer. This is
the minimal seam that enables it without forking the session state machine.

## Tests

`namidb-bolt` test suite green (45 tests), including two new ones that drive a
full handshake → HELLO → LOGON under `AuthPolicy::Custom` and assert accept /
reject. `cargo clippy -p namidb-bolt --no-deps -- -D warnings` clean.

## Summary
Migrated the theme system from hardcoded color values and inline CSS overrides to a centralized CSS custom properties (CSS variables) approach. This makes theme management more maintainable and enables dynamic theme switching without duplicating color definitions.

## Key Changes

- **Created theme files** (`src/themes/light.css`, `src/themes/dark.css`, `src/themes/warm.css`):
  - Each theme defines a complete set of CSS custom properties (`--color-gray-*`, `--color-blue-*`, `--color-indigo-*`)
  - Light theme uses standard Tailwind values
  - Dark theme inverts gray scale for dark surfaces while keeping blue accent colors
  - Warm theme replaces blue accent with rust/orange tones and uses slate-blue backgrounds

- **Updated `src/index.css`**:
  - Imports all three theme files at the top
  - Replaced 150+ lines of hardcoded warm theme overrides with CSS variable references
  - Simplified body styling to use `rgb(var(--color-*))` pattern
  - Consolidated form element styling (inputs, selects, textareas) to use variables
  - Removed duplicate theme-specific rules in favor of variable inheritance

- **Updated `tailwind.config.js`**:
  - Extended color definitions to reference CSS custom properties
  - Generated dynamic color scales (gray, blue, indigo) using `rgb(var(--color-*) / <alpha-value>)` pattern
  - Enables opacity modifiers (e.g., `bg-blue-600/30`) to work correctly with CSS variables

## Implementation Details

- Colors are stored as RGB triplets without `rgb()` wrapper (e.g., `"59 130 246"`) to support opacity modifiers
- Theme switching works by toggling `html.dark` or `html.warm` class; CSS variables automatically resolve to theme-specific values
- Warm theme's rust/orange accent (`#A35139`, `#FFB162`) replaces all blue color references while maintaining the same semantic structure
- Form elements use fallback styling with CSS variables for consistent appearance across themes

Adds a `workflow_dispatch` job to delete the pre-rename workers **`clickhouse-monitor`** and **`clickhouse-monitor-mcp`**, now orphaned after the `chmonitor-*` rename + apex cutover to `chmonitor-landing`.

## Why

The old workers still hold account-level **cron-trigger slots** (the account caps at 5), which blocked the `chmonitor-dash` deploy (CF error 10072 — see #1380), and the old MCP worker still answers the stale `chmonitor.dev/api/mcp*` route (503). Deleting them frees the slots and removes the stale route.

**Safe:** bound D1/R2/KV are account-level resources referenced by id and shared with the renamed workers, so deleting the old *workers* does not delete that data.

```
gh workflow run decommission-old-workers.yml -f confirm=DELETE
```

After it succeeds, restore the dashboard health-sweep cron (`crons = ["*/5 * * * *"]` in `apps/dashboard/wrangler.toml`) in a follow-up PR.

author: chrisgeo
body:
## Summary
Aligns the `test` job in `.github/workflows/tests.yml` from `node-version: 25` to `node-version: 22`.

## Root cause
The `test` job (`ci` tier = `next build` + the full Playwright suite against one shared `next dev` server) intermittently wedges after ~146 tests, cascading later specs to `net::ERR_ABORTED` (surfaced on #555; full RCA in CHAOS-2041). The **identical** standalone `E2E Tests` job runs the same `ci/run_tests.sh e2e` and is reliably green — and it runs on **Node 22 LTS**, while this job runs on **Node 25** (non-LTS "current"). The build memory is reclaimed when `next build` exits, so the persistent differentiator between the wedging job and the passing one is the Node runtime version. Node 22 LTS is also the platform standard.

## Why minimal
Surgical, **gating-preserving** (e2e stays in the `test` contract — unlike moving it to a separate job). A speculative dev-server heap bump was considered but dropped to keep the change to the single most-likely, lowest-risk variable.

## Verification caveat (important)
The `changes` filter that gates this job does **not** include `.github/workflows/**`, so this workflow-only PR will **not** run the suite on its own CI — it's validated on the next PR that touches `src/`/`tests/`/`ci/` (e.g. #561). If the wedge recurs on Node 22, the documented fallback in CHAOS-2041 is to move the e2e tier out of the `ci` job (the dedicated `E2E Tests` job already covers it) and/or shard the suite.

CI/config-only change — no `src/` change (governance gate N/A), no rendered UI (no screenshots).

Closes CHAOS-2041

## Dogfood/hardening of the integrated researcher run path (PM interim mission)

Tracing the now-complete run path (#154 budget + #160 cliPath/no-swallow + RESEARCH-11 depth/escalate/ceiling + resume-on-confirm) surfaced two real issues, both about **honestly surfacing run outcomes**:

### 1. `ceiling-reached` ≠ empty (the failed≠empty class, one layer on)
A **Run-now refused by the per-Instance ceiling** (RESEARCH-11) returned `{sourceIds:[], note}` with no flag → `runActiveResearcherNow` reported `'no-finding'` → the UI said *"no new finding this pass."* A **rate-limit pause masquerading as an empty result** — exactly the dishonesty the team just fixed in #160 for failures.
- `runResearcher` now flags **`ceilingReached`**; `RunResearcherResult` (+ IPC type) + the Run-now path + the view surface it distinctly: *"Paused — research rate limit reached for now."*
- The data-layer distinction is also a **prerequisite for #65's typed report** (found/nothing/failed/escalation/ceiling must be distinguishable in the result).

### 2. Dev-jargon in the Researchers UI
`lastRunFromEvent` surfaces the raw audit slug, so the new events (`research-failed` / `escalated` / `ceiling-reached`) + pre-existing `no-finding` rendered as **kebab-case** in the last-run line — a dev-jargon leak in a user surface.
- New **`researcherOutcomeLabel`** maps each to a Principal-facing label ("run failed" / "paused — needs your review" / "paused — rate limit reached" / "no new findings" / "found sources"). The labels also feed #65's report copy.

### Regression tests (fail-before / pass-after)
- `researchRun.test` — ceiling pass → `ceilingReached:true` (not a bare no-finding); an admitted pass isn't flagged.
- `researchersPanel.test` — label map covers every outcome kind, no slug leak, defensive fallback.
- `researchersView.test` — run-now ceiling reads PAUSED (not "no new finding"); last-run shows the friendly label, never the raw slug.

## What

Adds per-IP rate limiting to the unauthenticated auth endpoints via [`django-ratelimit`](https://django-ratelimit.readthedocs.io) (Redis-backed in production):

| Endpoint | Limit |
|---|---|
| login | 5 / min |
| password reset request | 5 / hour |
| registration | 10 / hour |

Decorators use `block=False`, so each view returns a friendly response when the limit is hit instead of a bare 403:
- **login** → JSON `429` (the login modal already consumes JSON)
- **reset / register** → re-rendered form with a non-field error message

## Why

Found in codebase audit (top finding #2). Login allowed unlimited credential brute-forcing; password-reset and registration each fire an outbound email per request → email-bombing of arbitrary addresses + Brevo API cost abuse.

## Notes

- The test/e2e settings use `DummyCache`, under which `django-ratelimit` is a no-op — **the existing suite is unaffected**.
- New tests (`core/tests/views/test_rate_limiting.py`) opt into a real in-memory cache to exercise the throttling path.
- `django_ratelimit.*` added to the mypy missing-imports override (matches the existing `wagtail.*` entry).

Fixes #9396

## Summary

- **Removed automatic ad-hoc fallback**: electron-builder previously signed arm64/universal macOS apps with an ad-hoc identity (`-`) when no signing certificate was found. This automatic fallback, combined with the default `hardenedRuntime: true`, caused macOS to reject the app at launch due to a Team ID mismatch between the ad-hoc-signed main binary and the pre-signed Electron frameworks bundled inside the app.

  Behavior now aligns with electron-forge: when no valid certificate is found, signing is skipped for all architectures. Ad-hoc signing is still supported but must be opted into explicitly by setting `mac.identity: "-"`.

- **Added `isHardenedRuntimeEnabledForSigning` static helper**: extracted the `hardenedRuntime` defaults logic (on by default for non-MAS, off by default for MAS) into a directly-testable static method on `MacTargetHelper`.

body:
## What & why

Reaping an idle agent stops it and removes its worktree, but deliberately leaves its records behind for history. Over a long-running project that debris accumulates. This adds an **opt-in full purge** that erases every trace of a reaped agent so the workspace can be cleared.

A purge removes, for the agent:
- mail (sent + received)
- events (run-scoped)
- queued merges
- the on-disk `.agentplate/agents/<name>/` state dir (identity CV + applied-skills)
- the task spec — only once no sibling session still references its `taskId`
- the session row itself

## Changes

- **New orchestration** `purgeAgentData` (`src/sessions/purge.ts`) returning a counted `PurgeReport`; best-effort and isolated per step (one store failing never aborts the rest). The state-dir removal is path-guarded to stay inside `.agentplate/agents/`.
- **Backing store deletion APIs**: `SessionStore.deleteSession`, `EventStore.deleteByAgent`, `MergeQueue.deleteByAgent` (mail already had `purge({ agent })`).
- **Wired into** `reapIdleSessions` via `ReapOptions.purge` — opens the aux stores once per sweep, attaches the report to each `ReapedAgent`. The non-purge path is unchanged.
- **Surfaces**:
  - `agentplate reap --purge` (opt-in; existing `reap` behavior preserved)
  - `agentplate stop <agent> --purge` (implies worktree removal)
  - `agents.purgeOnReap` config (default `false`), honored by the `serve` idle-reaper loop
  - a gated toggle in `agentplate setup`

## Compatibility

Plain `reap` / `serve` behavior is **unchanged** — reaping still keeps records for history by default. Full erasure is strictly opt-in via `--purge` / `purgeOnReap`, consistent with the codebase's mark-terminal-over-delete default.

## Tests

Real temp-git + SQLite throughout (no mocks): new delete-API tests per store, a dedicated `purge.test.ts` (verifies nothing remains, a sibling agent is untouched, shared specs survive until the last session, empty-case resilience), and reaper-level purge/non-purge integration tests.

Gates green: `bun test` (683 pass / 0 fail), `tsc --noEmit`, `biome check`.

body:
## 目的

`selfhost::parser::format::format_source` real-path 接続 (#1162) の次段階として、formatter helper `index_after_import` を compiled path に載せる (#1165)。`index_after_import` 専用の dispatch ではなく、汎用 token-array scan while capability として実装する。

## 追加した generic loop capability

既存の bounded-counter while lowering (`lower_multi_while_statement`) を、`index_after_import` 固有でない形で拡張した:

- **Parameter/local-seeded induction variable**: `var index = import_index;` が loop-head phi を preheader edge で param/local の SSA 値から seed できるようになった。`MirWhileStmt` に `induction_init_var` を追加し、`find_induction_init` が Int literal または plain Var 名 init を受理する（それ以外の init shape は明示 error）。`resolve_let_value_kizu_type` が Var 初期化子の型を参照先 parameter（または outer local）から解決する。
- **While-body locals threading**: body の `let token = try tokens.get(index);` が後続 body 文の読む local を bind するため、拡張された `locals_spec` を top-level statement loop と同様に body 全体へ thread する。これがないと body call 引数（`is_semicolon_token(token)`）の型解決が失敗する。
- **i64 error-union early returns**: error-union 関数内の if-then `return <expr>;` が値を `%kizu.error.<T>` success value に wrap するようになった（`append_multi_if_return_expr`、if-index 接尾辞付き SSA 名）。既存の trailing-return wrap / ReturnBool wrap と同じ方式で、複数 early-return が衝突しない。

## compiled path に載った formatter helper

`selfhost::parser::format::index_after_import` を format closure (IR + backend) に seed。body は value-receiver `Array<Token>` param の `tokens.len()` / `tokens.get(index)` を読み、`is_semicolon_token`（catalog BFS で解決）と `lexer::is_eof`（exact cross-module external callee）を呼び、loop 早期 exit で i64 を返す。

生成される `@kizu_selfhost__parser_format_index_after_import -> %kizu.error.i64` を format structural gate の seed list と stage0-native backend artifact gate で固定した。生成 LLVM（抜粋）:

```llvm
loop1_head:
  %index = phi i64 [ %import_index, %loop1_preheader ], [ %index_next, %loop1_latch ]
  %t1 = call i64 @kizu_rt_array_len(%kizu.owned %tokens)
  %t2 = icmp slt i64 %index, %t1
  br i1 %t2, label %loop1_body, label %loop1_exit
  ...
if1002_then:
  %t7 = add i64 %index, 1
  %if1002_retexpr_val = insertvalue %kizu.error.i64 ... i64 %t7, 1
  ret %kizu.error.i64 %if1002_retexpr_val
```

## まだ残る blocker

`format_source` closure の残りの loop helper には別 capability が必要:

- `index_after_leading_imports`: loop-carried i64 を try-call で再代入する shape (`index = try index_after_import(tokens, index);`) を phi latch に流す必要がある。現在の constant-step latch model では表現できない。
- `leading_import_indices` / `sort_import_indices` / `append_sorted_imports`: mutable `Array<i64>.append` / `Array<i64>.set` と short-circuit while が必要。

## 触っていないもの

- `parse_format_alloc`（hand-written 形式の bounded formatter）は拡張していない。format structural gate の `parseFormatAllocMaxLines` / `parser_format` 非参照アサーションで維持。
- formatter golden は変更なし。
- source literal / fixture path dispatch / static artifact branch / Go fallback / hidden fallback は追加なし。
- `MirTokenizeStmt` 的な name-special dispatch や helper 固有 static LLVM は追加なし（value-loop structural gate で維持）。
- helper ごとの手書き metadata table は追加なし（catalog-driven のまま）。

## 検証

- `go run ./cmd/kizu check selfhost` → `check: ok`
- `go test ./cmd/kizu -run 'TestSelfhost.*(Compiled|Mir|Backend|Runtime|Artifact|Package|Format)' -count=1` → ok
- `go test ./cmd/kizu -count=1` → ok (64s)
- `KIZU_RUN_SELFHOST_GATES=1 go test ./cmd/kizu -run 'TestSelfhostBackendArtifactGate$' -count=1` → ok（生成 LLVM が clang build + link + smoke 成功）

author: noumenon-ai
body:
## What this is

Roadmap item #1 — **outcome monitoring**. A fix that passed once can quietly break later. `automaxfix monitor` re-runs the verification of every previously-passed ticket and raises a fresh ticket if the failure has returned.

## How it works

- `find_monitorable` selects tickets with status `passed` and a stored `verification_command`.
- `monitor_once` re-runs each verification via the sanitized minimal-env runner (`run_command(..., allow_full_env=False)`); a non-zero exit (or timeout) is a regression.
- On regression it creates a NEW linked ticket: `source=regression`, `regressed_from=<original id>`, copying the original's verification/reproduction/suspected-files. The original ticket is never mutated, so "fixed then regressed" history is preserved.
- New `Ticket.regressed_from` field (round-trips in to_dict/from_dict; defaults None for old tickets).
- `automaxfix monitor [--since-days N]` — one-shot; schedule via cron or `watch`. No daemon.

Because it re-runs the exact signal that proved the fix, a regression cannot be hidden by editing a test.

## End-to-end verified

Ran a live smoke (init -> scan -> check -> monitor): a seeded passed ticket whose verification now exits non-zero produced a regression ticket with `regressed_from` set to the original and the carried verify command.

## Scope held

No daemon/scheduler, no auto-fixing in monitor (detect + ticket only), no notifications, no changes to run/scan/check/watch/scanners/safety.

## Docs

README updated (monitor section, CLI entry, "works today" table now lists outcome monitoring) and ROADMAP updated (monitor outcome marked shipped one-shot; near-term reordered).

## Tests

`101 -> 108` passing. `tests/test_monitor.py` covers monitorable filtering, non-regression, regression + linked-ticket creation, `--since-days` window (injected clock), sanitized-env isolation, and `regressed_from` round-trip. ruff + black clean.

# Overview Extends the server-upgrade-automation pipeline to triage Jellyfin **pre-release** builds — release candidates and `unstable`/`master` datestamped builds — *before* a stable release lands, and codifies standing up a new `apiVersion` tier when one is warranted. The mechanical layer is version-string-agnostic and channel-aware; the `/server-upgrade` skill gains an ephemeral pre-release path (local handoff, no GitHub issues) and a sibling `/new-api-version` scaffolding skill. A run of this pipeline against `10.11.10 → master` is what tells us, proactively, whether the next Jellyfin server breaks anything JellyRock ships — see the run output below. The branch also folds in audit-driven hardening of the triage path and a small shared-helper extraction. ## Changes - **Pre-release channel support (mechanical layer)** — `spec-fetch.cjs` accepts `-rcN`/`-betaN`/`-alphaN` suffixes + unstable datestamps and routes datestamps to `/openapi/unstable/`; `signals-fetch.cjs` resolves the latest *immutable* datestamped master build (never the mutable rolling pointer); `version-boundaries.cjs` resolves an RC to its base tier and a datestamp to the active tier; `findings-candidates.js` accepts the literal `unstable`/`master`, pins + echoes the resolved datestamp into the report + cache filename. - **`/server-upgrade` pre-release path** — ephemeral fetch, local handoff, **no GitHub issues filed**, re-diffable as the pre-release evolves; explicitly skips the stable path's label/digest steps and frames breaking findings as the new-tier worklist. - **`/new-api-version` skill** — guided V3/V4/V5 tier scaffolding wrapping the canonical versioning recipe, keeping `jellyfin-version-boundaries.yml` and `resolveApiVersion()` in lockstep. - **`lint:apiversion-consistency` static lint** — parses `resolveApiVersion()` with the BrighterScript AST and fails if its guards drift from the boundary map. Offline + network-free; wired into `_lint-floor-system.yml` CI and the aggregate `lint`. - **Rename-candidate emission** — `spec-diff.js` `param-removed`/`field-removed` now carry `renameCandidates` (always present, possibly `[]`): same-operation/same-schema additions that could be the rename. An empty list is the load-bearing signal that a removal is very likely genuine. - **Audit-driven triage hardening** — Step 2 edge case #8 (removal-vs-rename must be *resolved*, not hedged); Step 2.8 (genuine-removal ≠ behavior-change — honor-check the FROM-version before concluding a behavior break); a citation-depth floor (every usage / non-usage claim must pin the exact `file:line`, not just the file). Verbatim from the `2026-06-02` run against the resolved master build `20260531151854`. **Result: No breaking changes for what JellyRock ships.** 6 candidates investigated → 5 skip, 1 monitor (minor opportunity). 5 floor-known (not investigated). 0 suppressed. **No new `apiVersion` tier is warranted** — zero genuine `>= N`-needing breaks. | # | Finding | Verdict | Why | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | `param-removed GET /Audio/{itemId}/stream` — `breakOnNonKeyFrames` | **skip** | JellyRock never sends this query param. body:
**42 days to first offer is wrong because the process tracker was stale.** The AI computes weeks-to-LOI as `(week 12 LOI receipt) − (current task week)`. With stored `currentTaskId = "cim_deliver"` (week 6), that gives `12 − 6 = 6 weeks = 42 days`. But you have **3 buyers at chemistry stage** (process week 9+), so LOI is actually only ~3 weeks = 21 days away. The stored `currentTaskId` is a field the user has to click through to advance, and it had fallen behind reality.

**Fix.** Server-side, derive the effective `currentTaskId` from actual buyer state on every rescan. Use the **more-advanced** of `(stored, derived)` — so explicit user intent isn't overridden if you manually advanced past the derived position.

Mapping (least to most advanced):
- any `closed` → `close` (week 22)
- one buyer at LOI+ → `select` (week 14)
- multiple at LOI → `lois` (week 12)
- any at `chemistry` stage → `process_letter` (week 11)
- `chemistry_date` set on any nda buyer → `chemistry` (week 9)
- `cim_delivered` set on any nda buyer → `initial_qa` (week 7)
- any at `nda` → `cim_deliver` (week 6)
- only `outreach` → `outreach` (week 5)

For your current state (3 chemistry, 1 NDA+CIM, 1 outreach), the effective task becomes `process_letter` (week 11). LOI is `12 − 11 = 1 week ≈ 7 days`. Projected offer should compress from `Jul 2026 (42d)` to around early June 2026.

`PROMPT_VERSION` bumped `14 → 15`.

**On the verdict "always wrong" complaint:** the verdict cites the AI's own probability output. With the time anchor now reflecting actual deal state, the AI should produce sharper close/offer estimates and a tighter verdict. The ranking judgment between Trucordia / Oakbridge / Kelly is still Opus's call — that's the model's job. If you genuinely disagree with the model on a specific buyer, the chat `override_probability` tool exists.

## Test plan
- [ ] After redeploy + rescan, `Projected offer` collapses from `Jul 2026` toward `Jun 2026` (or earlier if multiple buyers are at chemistry)
- [ ] The `XXd Xh Xm to first offer` countdown matches the new estimate
- [ ] Footer shows `prompt v15`
- [ ] If the user manually advances `currentTaskId` past the derived value (e.g., to `select`), the stored value still wins

# Describe the pull request

Thank you for contributing to the project!
Please use this template to help us handle your PR smoothly.

## What

Disallow the `border`, `background`, and `font` shorthands via Stylelint’s `property-disallowed-list`, and rewrite the existing usages as longhands.

## Why

These three are *facet-bundling* shorthands: each one bundles independent sub-properties that, in our system, map to their own design tokens (e.g. `border-width` / `border-style` / `border-color`).

Two problems follow from using the shorthand:

- It silently resets sibling sub-properties to their initial values (`border` resets `border-image`; `background` resets seven sub-properties). That’s an easy way to wipe a value set elsewhere.
- It hides the per-token structure and makes targeted overrides (e.g. a forced-colors block that only changes `border-color`) harder and riskier.

This extends the longhand/logical direction the config already takes — `margin`, `padding`, and `inset` are disallowed, `csstools/use-logical` is on, and `declaration-block-no-redundant-longhand-properties` is already turned off so longhands aren’t recombined.

## How

- Add `background`, `border`, and `font` to the existing `property-disallowed-list`.
- Convert the facet-bundle borders in Progress List and Switch to `border-color` / `border-style` / `border-width`.
- Convert the `border: none` resets (Avatar, `reset-button`, `reset-fieldset`) to `border-style: none`.
- Convert the Dialog backdrop’s `background:` to `background-color:` (and Storybook’s gradient to `background-image:`).
- Convert the six shorthand sites in Storybook’s docs/preview CSS.

## Scope notes

- **Kept as shorthand on purpose:** `gap`, `border-radius`, `flex`, `transition`, `animation`, `outline`, `text-decoration`, `place-*`. These either distribute one value across sides/corners (no per-token rationale) or are almost always atomic keywords (`flex: none`, `transition: none`) whose hand-written longhands would be more verbose and more error-prone — `property-disallowed-list` is value-blind, so banning them would catch those too.
- **Per-side border shorthands left alone** (`border-block-end`, `border-inline-start`, …): several are backed by a single composite token (e.g. `--ams-table-cell-border-block-end`, `--ams-field-invalid-border-inline-start`). Splitting them into longhands would require splitting those tokens — out of scope for a lint cleanup.

author: maorbril
body:
## Problem

A well-known bug: while `clauder wrap` is running and the user has typed into the Claude prompt but not yet sent it, the screen fills with `[watcher] N unread but CanInject=false, will retry` errors.

### Root cause

The message watcher logs via the standard `log` package, whose default output is **stderr**. In `wrap` mode stderr is the live terminal that Claude Code's TUI is drawing on — so every `log.Printf` scribbles directly over the screen.

The flood is triggered because `CanInject` stays false whenever the input buffer is non-empty:

```go
func (t *inputTracker) CanInject(idleTimeout time.Duration) bool {
    return len(t.buffer) == 0 && time.Since(t.lastKeystroke) > idleTimeout
}
```

The buffer only clears on Enter / Ctrl+U / Ctrl+C. So if the user types text but doesn't press Enter ("didn't send a message"), `CanInject` is false indefinitely, and the watcher logs the retry line **every tick** (every 5s) onto the TUI.

## Fix

1. **Redirect the standard logger to a file** (`$dataDir/wrap.log`, or `io.Discard` if it can't be opened) before starting the watcher, so no watcher/diagnostic output ever reaches the terminal.
2. **Throttle the retry log** to once per pending batch (reset when the batch changes, clears, or is injected) instead of every tick.

Fix #1 alone resolves the visible symptom; #2 keeps the log file clean and avoids the underlying spin-logging.

## Testing

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./cmd/`, `go test ./cmd/` all pass.
- `gofmt` clean.

## What

Broadens the activity log to a **complete API-action trail** — on top of the existing rich, per-action audit records.

An **outermost HTTP middleware** records every **mutating** (`POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE`) request under `/api` as a generic **`api_call`** audit entry capturing:
- **actor** (resolved by the auth guard from the HA identity / local owner),
- **method**, **path**, and the final **status code**.

Design notes:
- **Reads excluded** — GET/HEAD/OPTIONS aren't logged (dashboard polling etc. would be pure noise); "actions" = mutations.
- **No request body logged** (privacy — bodies can contain financial data); only method/path/status.
- **Best-effort** — wrapped in try/except so an audit write can never break the request; **skipped while the DB is locked**.
- Action label is the fixed string `api_call` so the Logs **action-filter dropdown stays small**; method/path/status live in `details` (the Logs page already renders details generically, e.g. `method: POST · path: /api/transactions/5 · status: 200`).
- It's the outermost middleware, so it sees both the actor (set by the inner auth guard) and the final response status.

Failed/blocked attempts (e.g. a read-only role's 403) are captured too, with their status — useful as a security signal. The retention engine can age these out like any audit row.

## Tests
`test_logs`: mutating calls produce `api_call` entries with actor+method+path+status; GETs are **not** logged; `api_call` appears in the action-filter list. ## ast-grep 0.43.0 recipe for "node without preceding comment"

PR #16 noted that "negative-precedes relations are awkward in ast-grep 0.43.0." Verified during smoke that the correct primitive is **\`not.follows\`** (NOT \`not.precedes\`):

\`\`\`yaml
rule:
  kind: type_declaration
  has:
    kind: type_spec
    has:
      kind: interface_type
  not:
    follows:
      kind: comment

author: jvoegele
body:
## Summary

Adds **exception wrapping / chaining** to Errata. Application code can catch a lower-level failure — an exception from a subsystem or external library, or an arbitrary error value — and translate it into a structured Errata error of its own *without discarding the original*.

This follows the **single-cause (causal chain) model** used by Java, Python, Go, Rust, and .NET, rather than the aggregation/classification model of Splode — Errata's per-error, named, structured types complement Splode rather than competing with it.

## What's included

- **New `Errata.Cause` struct** (`kind` / `value` / `stacktrace`) — the mirror of `Errata.Env`: `Env` records *where the error was wrapped*, `Cause` records *what was wrapped and where it originally occurred*.
- **Generated `wrap/1,2` macro** on every error module — equivalent to `create/1` plus a cause. Captures the wrap-site `__ENV__`, and when given `stacktrace: __STACKTRACE__`, preserves the original error's stacktrace.
- **`:cause` param** accepted by `new/1`, `create/1`, and `raise/2` (normalized into an `Errata.Cause`).
- **Accessors**: `Errata.cause/1` (immediate cause), `Errata.root_cause/1` (walks the chain to the deepest cause), `Errata.format_chain/1` (renders the full `Caused by:` chain for logging). `Exception.message/1` stays clean — the chain only surfaces via `format_chain/1`.
- **Serialization**: `to_map/1` and JSON include the cause, recursing into wrapped Errata errors and rendering standard exceptions by type and message. The raw stacktrace is omitted from JSON, consistent with `Errata.Env.to_map/1`.
- The cause may be **any term** (an Errata error, a standard exception, or a plain value such as the `reason` from an `{:error, reason}` tuple), consistent with how errors are represented on the BEAM.
- Behaviour `@macrocallback`s for `wrap`, a "Wrapping errors" README section (with a runnable doctest), CHANGELOG entry, and version bump to **0.10.0**.

## Example

```elixir
try do
  Jason.decode!(payload)
rescue
  e ->
    {:error, MyApp.InvalidPayload.wrap(e, stacktrace: __STACKTRACE__, reason: :malformed_json)}
end
```

- `mix test` → **11 doctests, 61 tests, 0 failures** (18 new tests + a new README doctest)

body:
Fixes **B-54** — Rolex Explorer 14270 listings showing model "Submariner". The reported typo turned out to sit on top of two deeper bugs.

## Root causes
1. **Orphaned Explorer refs.** The `Explorer / Explorer II` model line stored its references under `**Refs (Explorer)**` / `**Refs (Explorer II)**` — labels `parse_index` doesn't recognise (it only honours the literal `**Refs**:` key, and *overwrites* on a second one). So the entire Explorer ref set was unindexed (`refs: []`), and `14270` only matched because it had been parked under `Submariner` with an `(n/a—Explorer)` note as a workaround — the wrong line.
2. **Brand-blind matching.** `match_against_index` returned the *first* candidate token's index hit. A leading **year** that collides with another brand's reference (`1991` → Cartier Panthère ref 1991) won, and merge.py's cross-pollination guard then rejected the whole hit → empty `model_line` for "1991 Rolex Explorer 14270". (Brand resolution to Rolex was fine all along; the reported "Submariner" was year-dependent behaviour.)

## Fix
- Merge Explorer refs onto one `**Refs**:` line — also indexes the long-orphaned `6098`/`124270`/`224270`/`216570`/… set for the first time. Remove `14270` from Submariner.
- Make `match_against_index` **brand-aware**: with a brand hint it skips tokens that resolve only to other brands and keeps scanning for a same-brand ref. Optional arg; the ~15 editorial callers pass no brand → unchanged.
- `model_line` is not persisted in `state.json`, so the next scrape re-tags all **29** affected rows (Falco/MVV/Bulang/Huntington/Tropical Watch) to Explorer automatically — verified locally.

## Tests
New `tests/test_reference_match.py` (4 cases: 14270→Explorer not Submariner; Explorer refs indexed; leading-year no longer shadows the real ref; brandless behaviour preserved). Full suite **31 passed**.

## Follow-up
Spun off **B-57**: a sweep found same-brand, different-family ref collisions worth a domain pass with Mark (Patek 5236P, Cartier WJTA0001, IWC IW5004, UG Compax refs, …). Cross-brand collisions are already neutralised by the guard; layered same-family entries are intentional. Logged, not auto-edited (respects the Camaro/Carrera note).

## Summary

Add a `LOG_ANON` parameter that shifts all lat/lng fields in onboard DataFlash logs by a random per-boot offset, preserving flight-path shape while hiding absolute location.

## Description

When `LOG_ANON=1`, all latitude/longitude fields (format type `L`) in onboard logs are offset by a random value generated at boot. The shape of the flight path is preserved but the absolute location is hidden.

The anonymization is applied centrally in `WriteBlock`, `WriteCriticalBlock`, `WriteBlock_first_succeed`, and the `Backend::Write` (variadic) path by scanning the format string for `L` fields and offsetting them in-place. body:
## Problem

`_binarySearchMaxSize` brackets the max openable position size by exponentially growing a probe (`high *= 100`) until a size is non-openable. For some tokenIds an oversized probe exceeds the protocol's liquidity bounds and reverts with `LiquidityTooHigh` **before** the account ever becomes insolvent, which aborts the entire search and bubbles the revert to callers.

This breaks panoptic-v2-core's I9 self-liquidation fuzz/regression tests (e.g. `testFuzz_I9_randomTokenId_selfLiquidationNoProfit`), which call `getMaxPositionSizeBounds` to pick a position size.

## Fix

Wrap `isAccountSolvent` in `try/catch` inside `_canOpenSize` and treat a reverting probe as a non-openable size. The search then continues toward the true, solvency-bounded maximum instead of propagating the revert. No behavioral change for probe sizes within liquidity bounds.
